name: CaptionCall Mobile
oneLine: Sorenson's US phone-call caption app, free through the FCC for eligible people with hearing loss; Sorenson also provides a captioned home phone.

platforms.detail: On the App Store (iPhone and iPad, with call alerts on Apple Watch), Google Play and the Amazon Appstore for Fire tablets. Sorenson also provides a CaptionCall home phone with a caption screen.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 16.0 or later. Sorenson's CaptionCall Mobile page says iOS 15 or later and Android 9 or later.

roomCaptions.detail: CaptionCall says the app only captions calls that go through your CaptionCall number. None of its pages describe captioning people in the same room.

groupConversations.detail: You can merge a second call into a 3-way call, and all parties are captioned. Nothing is described for groups in the same room.

languages.detail: CaptionCall can caption calls in English and Spanish. Spanish captions were added to the app in 2023.

offline.text: No, needs Wi-Fi or mobile data
offline.detail: Calls are captioned anywhere with Wi-Fi or mobile data. A 911 call also needs a data connection.

speakerLabels.text: Your side and the caller's, in colours
speakerLabels.detail: Both sides of the call are captioned, each in its own coloured text bubble. You can turn off the captions of your own voice.

translation.detail: No CaptionCall page describes translating speech from one language into another.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, on the phone, by default
saveTranscripts.detail: Call transcripts are saved to the History tab by default and stored on the device. Sorenson says only you can access them.

export.text: Share a transcript from call history
export.detail: Open a call in History, tap Share Transcript and choose how to export it.

fileUpload.detail: No CaptionCall page mentions transcribing an uploaded audio or video file.

summaries.detail: No CaptionCall page mentions summaries of calls.

customWords.detail: No CaptionCall page mentions adding your own words or names.

display.detail: A slider changes the caption size, also during a call. Captions can stay on screen in a small window over other apps, and the app has a dark mode.

soundAlerts.detail: No alerts for sounds around you are described. Incoming calls can show on a smartwatch.

phoneCalls.detail: CaptionCall captions incoming and outgoing calls, 3-way calls, voicemail and 911 calls. Call forwarding and My Caller ID let you keep using your own number.

videoCalls.detail: No CaptionCall page describes captioning Zoom, FaceTime or other video calls.

mediaOnDevice.detail: No CaptionCall page describes captioning videos or other media playing on the phone.

humanCaptioners.text: Home phone: yes; mobile app: no
humanCaptioners.detail: On the CaptionCall home phone, a live captioning agent connects to each call. CaptionCall Mobile doesn't use live agents: its captions are automatic.

signLanguage.detail: CaptionCall shows text captions. Sorenson, the same company, offers ASL interpreting for phone calls through its separate Sorenson VRS service.

privacy.text: Cloud; call audio not kept on servers
privacy.detail: The privacy policy says call audio and transcription are not kept by Sorenson or its providers, and transcripts are saved on your phone. It also says information it collects may be used to help train its machine learning or AI models.

account.detail: Sign-up asks for your cell number, email, your details as on your government ID and your home address, and you self-certify your hearing loss. The FCC says IP CTS providers ask for your date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number.

availability.detail: CaptionCall and CaptionCall Mobile are available in the United States only. The app was not found in the UK, Canadian, Mexican, Australian or German App Stores.

freePlan.detail: No cost and no subscription for people with hearing loss who need captions to use the phone.

price.detail: The app is free on the App Store and Google Play, and Sorenson says there is no subscription (US, October 2026). The CaptionCall home phone is also provided at no cost.

accessibilityFunding.detail: The FCC lists CaptionCall, LLC with conditional certification to provide IP CTS, with a Sorenson contact. The FCC's fund pays Sorenson for each minute of captions.

strengths.text: Free for eligible US users with hearing loss, with no subscription: the FCC's fund pays for the captions.
Captions phone calls, 3-way calls, voicemail and 911 calls, and lets you keep your own number through call forwarding and My Caller ID.
Sorenson also provides eligible users a CaptionCall home phone at no cost, with delivery, setup and a live captioning agent on calls.
Works with Bluetooth hearing aids, AirPods and other headphones.

limits.text: It captions phone calls only: the app captions calls that go through your CaptionCall number.
Only available in the United States, for registered users with hearing loss.
Calls are captioned in English and Spanish only.
It needs Wi-Fi or mobile data, and calls to your usual number aren't captioned until you set up call forwarding.

sources.title: CaptionCall (App Store, US)
quotes: CaptionCall Mobile empowers deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals to make and receive phone calls with instant live captions.
No more landlines. CaptionCall Mobile goes where you go, allowing you to make and receive captioned calls from your mobile device anywhere with WiFi or mobile data service.

Fast, accurate, and easy, CaptionCall automatically transcribes both sides of your conversation in a customizable easy-to-read format, using advanced voice to text for deaf and hard-of-hearing that is 100% private and secure.
You'll have quick access to your saved contacts, captioned voicemail and voicemail alerts, and can dial and receive calls from any phone number, just like your regular phone.
CaptionCall and CaptionCall Mobile are available in the United States only.
The CaptionCall phone and app remain the property of Sorenson in order to provide ongoing support, service, and upgrades.

sources.title: Does CaptionCall Work on a Cell Phone? Is It Really No Cost?
quotes: If you use CaptionCall Mobile, each side of the conversation displays in a colored text bubble.

When you make or receive a call using CaptionCall, a live captioning agent automatically connects to your call. The agent uses voice-recognition technology and manual corrections to turn your phone conversation into captions.

sources.title: Internet Protocol (IP) Captioned Telephone Service
quotes: Internet Protocol Captioned Telephone Service (IP CTS) is a form of telecommunications relay service (TRS) that permits an individual who can speak but who has difficulty hearing over the telephone to use a telephone and an Internet Protocol-enabled device via the Internet to simultaneously listen to the other party and read captions of what the other party is saying.

sources.title: New IP CTS Registration Requirements FAQs

Users must also provide a document with a U.S. address to verify that the user is located in the United States.

notes: Ownership: CaptionCall is Sorenson's. captioncall.com redirects to sorenson.com/captioncall/; Sorenson's privacy policy covers "Sorenson Communications, LLC; CaptionCall, LLC"; the Google Play developer is CaptionCall, LLC (Salt Lake City, UT); the FCC lists CaptionCall, LLC with conditional IP CTS certification and a Sorenson Communications compliance contact (page updated June 10, 2026). The App Store seller is still MachineGenius, Inc. (bundle id com.machingenius.olelo, copyright CaptionCall, LLC): the app was Olelo, which became part of Sorenson and was renamed CaptionCall Mobile in December 2023 (Sorenson press release; help article). Sorenson also provides CaptionCall home phones (landline/VoIP caption phones with a large screen) at no cost to eligible users, with delivery and installation, and says eligible users can have both. Conflicts: Sorenson's mobile page says iOS 15 or later and Android 9 or later, while the App Store lists iOS 16.0 or later; the store and site disclaimer says IP captioned telephone service "may use a live operator", while Sorenson's mobile page and blog say CaptionCall Mobile captions automatically without a live agent (the home phone uses live captioning agents). In-person use: no CaptionCall or Sorenson page found says anything about captioning people in the same room, either allowed or forbidden; the roomCaptions fact rests on the help centre saying the app only captions calls through the CaptionCall number, and on the FCC's description of IP CTS as captions of the other party on a call. Privacy: the privacy policy says call audio and transcription are not retained, and separately that collected information may be used to help train its machine learning or AI models (with aggregated or de-identified data); the App Store privacy label lists Identifiers as data used to track you. No In-App Purchases section on the App Store page and none shown on Google Play. The Amazon Appstore listing shows an older version (10.0.2401) and lists English only. FCC pages returned 403 to curl/WebFetch and were read in a browser. The Google Play page did not show a minimum Android version in the fetched HTML. Not found anywhere: translation, summaries, custom words, file upload, video calls, captioning media on the phone; these are not_stated. Customer quotes, store ratings and review counts on Sorenson's and the stores' pages were left out on purpose. The Sorenson blog post "Comparing Top Call Captioning Apps" (linked from its blog) returned 404 and was not used.
